title: Deep Cost Horizon: Preemptive GPU Selection and Dark-Pool Budget Guardrails
creator: Anika Rao
description: Problem: We currently route requests based on static priority bands and simple spot vs on-demand flags. During cross-regional demand spikes we see abrupt cost overruns or elevated latencies when high-priority routes exhaust on-demand headroom. Goal: Introduce a preemptive, predictively steered routing layer — the 'Deep Cost Horizon' — that (1) chooses GPU class and spot/on-demand mix using short-horizon demand forecasts, (2) enforces soft and hard budget guardrails per-tenant and per-route, and (3) transparently falls back to cheaper model variants (quantized / distilled) or degraded QoS policies when budget thresholds are hit. This ticket implements the core routing algorithm, policy primitives, and integration points with the autoscaler and billing guardrail service.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Default routing policy uses short-horizon demand prediction to select GPU family (A100/V100/RTX) and spot mix for 90% of requests in the test harness. 2) Soft budget caps trigger automated switch to fallbacks (quantized model variant or lower batch size) and are visible in Console during rollout. 3) Hard budget caps prevent allocation of new on-demand hours beyond configured commit and return 429 with a clear structured JSON reason and suggested remediation. 4) End-to-end latency for high-priority SLO routes must not regress >10% in 95th percentile under normal load. 5) E2E tests, canary, and rollout steps documented and linked in the ticket.
implementation_notes:
- Add new routing policy type 'predictive_cost_horizon' to the Smart Router.
- Integrate with Demand Predictor microservice via new API: /v1/predict?route=... (feature-flagged).
- Extend allocator to include 'preference_score' for GPU SKUs computed from predicted demand, spot eviction risk, and per-tenant budget headroom.
- Hook guardrail checks into billing-service's RSVP endpoint to atomically reserve budget when routing decisions allocate on-demand capacity.
- Create fallback mapping table: model family -> fallbacks (e.g., llama-65b-fp16 -> llama-65b-4bit-quant or llama-13b-distilled).
- Emit telemetry: routing.decisions.{chosen_sku, spot_fraction, fallback_used, predicted_peak} and billing.guardrail.{soft_trigger, hard_trigger}.
- Feature flags: ff.predictive_routing, ff.dark_pool_fallbacks.
milestones: Spike: evaluate demand predictor models and training data (completed)
Implement router changes + allocator hooks (in progress)
Integrate budget RSVP and guardrail checks (planned)
Canary rollout to 10% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants (planned)
Full rollout and monitor for 2 weeks (planned)
risks: Demand predictor mis-calibration could create oscillation between variants
Spot eviction bursts may expose model quality regressions if fallback pathways are untested
Atomicity between router and billing RSVP needs careful failure handling to avoid overcommit
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged merge to main behind ff.predictive_routing
Unit + integration tests and synthetic load tests in staging
Canary on non-enterprise tenants (10%) with realtime dashboards
If soft budget triggers exceed threshold or 95p latency regresses >10% -> rollback ff.predictive_routing
Progressively increase canary to 50% then 100% over 2 weeks
testing_notes:
- Add simulator that replays historical traffic with spot eviction traces to validate policy stability.
- Create canary evaluation notebook that reports cost delta and quality delta for fallback model variants using saved prompt sets.
- Add synthetic tests for RSVP failure modes (network partition, 500 errors) to ensure router falls back gracefully.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for allocator preference_score calculation
Integration test for billing RSVP with mock billing-service
E2E against staging that includes autoscaler behavior
Console shows guardrail state per-tenant during canary
